To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. Barter is an institution that mitigates incentive problems in debt repayment of countries with high debt to GNP ratios.

barter and counter-trade are efficient institutions that mitigate incentive problems that arise when technology is transferred to developing countries and when debt repayments of highly indebted countries are financed with exports.
barter and counter-trade contracts are efficient institutions that mitigate the incentive problems in technology trade, debt repayment, and capital flows.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of institutions in international trade, in particular, with the role of barter and counter trade as efficient institutions that help to overcome incentive problems in international technology transfer and debt repayment.
the role of incentives as a driving force of international trade.
the question of how institutions affect international trade flows.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the economic incentive approach has been very fruitful in the study of international trade.
the economic incentive models are not a panacea, and that there is no one-size-fits-all model that is appropriate for all situations.
barter is not a primitive and inefficient way of doing business, but a very sophisticated and efficient way of doing international trade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international trading system is characterized by a multitude of different trade contracts.
economic incentives are important for international trade.

incentives are important for international trade, that the institutions that mitigate incentive problems are efficient, and that the efficiency of the institutions can be measured in terms of the reduction in the transaction costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
international transactions are not only determined by the comparative advantage but also by the contractual hazards and the institutional arrangements that help to solve them.
the efficiency of international trade can be increased by designing institutions that create incentives for trade partners to fulfill their contracts.
incentives are an important determinant of international trade.
